trickyParts: The remembered reading index was the defect: an index names a position in a list another writer can prepend to. The selector names the passage instead - the words plus the text immediately before and after them, as the editor read it at selection - so a reading added in front changes nothing about the reader's own.

The resolution order keeps one deliberate asymmetry. Inside the block the reader selected in, a single reading of the quote is taken even when the words around it changed, because the block they chose holding their words once is their passage; that is what keeps the sentence-rewrite row green. Outside it, nothing is taken without matching surroundings.

The context cap is 32 characters each side, chosen by measuring this repository's own prose rather than picked: of 13,876 phrases that read more than once inside one block, 32 characters separate 90.4% of them, against 81.1% at 16 and 53.0% at 4. A unit test pins it against a shorter cap that would not separate the tester's two readings.

presentAt in packages/dispatch/e2e/compose-wait.e2e.ts asked for an exact second label, and the sampler loses a second now and then on a two-core box, which made my own round-1 row flake once here. It now reads the first sample at or after the second it asks about. That helper and the new ninth row are the only changes under packages/dispatch/e2e, and no row the tester wrote was touched.
